headline: Last session: Indian markets extended gains for third straight week despite Friday dip on inflation concerns.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 16 November.

why: Foreign institutional investor (FII) inflows drove weekly gains across Indian equities.
Global rotation trade out of overextended AI stocks redirected capital back toward Indian markets.
Inflation concerns weighed on investor sentiment, causing a 289-point decline in Sensex on Friday.
Lower crude oil prices provided relief and supported market sentiment earlier in the week.
whatHappening: Smallcap index jumped 3.6% and PSU Bank sector surged 7.5% during the week.
Max Estates received HARERA approval for a ₹4,000 crore luxury real estate project in Gurugram.
Alembic Pharma secured USFDA approval for lung cancer treatment drug Binimetinib.
Air purifier sales surged significantly in Delhi-NCR following a sharp deterioration in AQI levels.
summary:
Indian benchmark indices posted their third consecutive week of gains driven by persistent foreign fund buying.
Friday's session saw minor profit-taking and inflation worries drag the Sensex down by 289 points.
Stock-specific developments were highlighted by Max Estates' project approval and Alembic Pharma's USFDA clearance.
